title: Australia revenue estimate: basis and limitations

claims.text: Monetary basis: all estimates are expressed in constant 2025 USD, GDP-deflated, using a fixed 2025 exchange rate. The model does not simulate price or exchange-rate responses to the event, so results reflect only the modeled volume and fiscal-transmission channels in real terms.

Scope: the estimate is limited to agriculture, forestry and fishing value added and its conditional transmission into government revenue. Revenue is measured inclusive of grants. It is not a total-economy loss estimate and is not a sovereign default probability.

The risk measure is defined as neutral revenue minus event revenue, so gains are retained as signed negative values in mean estimates, while tail measures apply to the positive-part shortfall only. The mean and the tail metrics therefore are not directly comparable quantities.

Interpretation limits: the estimate is conditional on the official ENSO forecast vintage and does not constitute causal attribution of revenue outcomes to the event. The fiscal model relies on IMF total real GDP growth as an external non-agriculture growth proxy shared across cases, and the analysis is not causally identified.

Historical validation is conditional on realized inputs and latest revised history, so it does not demonstrate out-of-sample predictive skill for the forward revenue estimate; posterior convergence diagnostics alone cannot establish predictive skill.

limitations: The assessment bundle is flagged as having incomplete historical input provenance and is restricted to inspection; it is not recomputable.

The revenue estimate is conditional on the official forecast vintage and the modeled extension beyond the forecast horizon is not itself an official NOAA forecast; official forecasts are marginal, not joint.
Monetary values are constant 2025 USD, GDP-deflated, at a fixed 2025 exchange rate, with no modeled price or exchange-rate response.

Scope is limited to agriculture, forestry and fishing value added and conditional government revenue transmission, inclusive of grants; it is not a total-economy loss or a sovereign default probability.
The analysis is not causally identified; historical validation is conditional on realized inputs and latest revised history and does not establish predictive skill for forward estimates.
Mean losses are signed estimates retaining gains, while tail measures apply to the positive-part shortfall; the two should not be mixed when interpreting results.
